demand_source.title: Ohai: Your Household Manager for Calendars, To-Dos, Emails & Family Life
demand_source.supports: On a shipping family assistant's own page a parent says she sends it pictures of schedules and it puts them on the calendar, and the page's FAQ says it scans PDFs, photos and school newsletters.

caveats: Dates read from a photo can be wrong (a missing year, two children on one sheet, a blurry corner), so every proposal spells each date out in full and nothing is written until the parent says yes.
Until the calendar write is built the offer is reminders only; that part needs only photo and PDF reading (F002) and reminders (F007).

The yes before a reminder is a prompt rule; the approval before a calendar write is enforced by the hook. On iMessage that makes a calendar write two steps: the yes to the proposal, then a typed /approve line carrying the request's id, within ten minutes.

The tap-to-add calendar file is unconfirmed: the one report found is of a calendar file that came through Gmail and opened in Files on iOS 18 with no option to add it, so it is tested on both parents' phones before anything is built for it.
For one event on a poster a recent iPhone can already offer to add it from the camera; Happy's part is a sheet with many dates, a PDF, a day-before reminder and the calendar both parents share.
Typing /approve in iMessage Basic mode to resolve the approval was not tested end to end.
The calendar write applies only if the calendar decision lands on Google, and neither the write wrapper nor the calendar-file plugin exists yet.

A list of school deadlines or a season schedule is one more dated document: rows are stored (F031) only after a yes, and the week-ahead brief (F014) reads open school deadlines from there. A lunch menu can be read and asked about like any other photo, but no brief reads stored menu rows, and Happy is never the allergy authority.

Plugin approvals are asked once per tool call, the approval text is capped at 512 characters, and a prompt also offers 'allow always' unless the hook leaves it out. A season schedule is many events, so the write tool should take the whole confirmed list in one call, the approval text should give the count and the date range instead of every row, and the hook should offer only allow-once and deny.

demand_source.title: Multi-agent routing: family agent bound to a WhatsApp group
demand_source.supports: OpenClaw's own multi-agent guide gives, as a worked example, a dedicated family agent bound to a single group chat with mention gating and a tighter tool policy than a personal agent.

edits.how: groupPolicy allowlist with groupAllowFrom and a groups[chat_id] entry; bindings[] with peer kind group routes it to a stateless family-group agent; mention gating uses the agent name; `channels.imessage.historyLimit: 0`, so that group messages the helper skipped are not handed to it the next time it is named.
caveats: The roadmap's M1 milestone and its S1 channel-isolation baseline keep iMessage groups disabled. This entry re-opens them for one registered chat, with a sender allowlist and mention gating, so it is a change to that baseline for Tony to approve. OpenClaw's security guide calls a private room whose members you trust (team, family or friends) a normal deployment (gateway/security/access-control.md:29).

In Basic mode Happy can read and reply in a group but has no group actions such as renaming it or adding people (private-api.md:29), so a parent creates the group from a phone and Tony reads its chat id with imsg chats.
Both parents see every answer given in the group, so nothing from one parent's memory or mail belongs there; the group helper holds none.

A group that answers only when named still keeps the messages it skipped and adds them as context the next time Happy is named (channels/groups.md:547); the default window is 50 messages. Left on, what the two parents write to each other in the group would reach the cloud model in the same turn as web search results. The group history limit is therefore set to 0 (config-channels/mention-gating-and-history.md:61), so the helper sees only the message that names it.
unverified: Receiving and replying in a three-person group in Basic mode has not been tried live on this Mac; the docs warn that some multi-person threads arrive flagged as non-group unless the chat id is registered (access-control.md:152-153).
Whether a voice memo in the group can satisfy the mention gate on iMessage is not documented (audio.md:286 defers to channel docs).
The numeric chat id is unknown until the group is created and read with imsg chats.

That a history limit of 0 on the iMessage channel stops skipped group messages reaching the helper has not been tried on this Mac; the docs describe the window for all channels and show the key in the iMessage example config (config-channels/personal-messaging.md:172).
edits.safety: The group helper is a separate agent with no memory tools and no calendar, list or mail tools, so nothing held by one parent's own agent can surface in front of the other. Only the two parents' handles pass the group sender allowlist, only the one registered chat is admitted, and Happy answers only when it is named. By default a group that answers only when named keeps up to 50 skipped messages and hands them to the helper the next time it is named, which would put the parents' own conversation in the same turn as web search results; the group history limit is set to 0 so that the helper sees only the message that names it. Web search results are outside content, and the helper can reply only in this group.

demand_source.title: Ohai.ai features: AI calendar management
demand_source.supports: A shipping family assistant's own feature page says it scans the user's connected calendars and flags overlapping events, sold as conflict detection that avoids double bookings.

edits.how: A zero-model command job (`--command-argv`) every few hours, inside the allowed hours only, runs a host script under the happy user: `gog calendar conflicts` (or `freebusy`) across the shared family calendar and the two parents' calendars, compares against a seen-id state file, and prints `NO_REPLY` when nothing is new. To keep each parent's data separate, the script uses one read-only credential that sees the family calendar in full and each parent's own calendar as free/busy only (Google's 'See only free/busy (hide details)' share), so the message names the family-calendar event and says only 'busy' for personal ones. The docs show a single `--to` target per job, so plan one job per parent or the parents' group chat once F006 exists; the follow-up question reuses the ask-and-relay step of G009.
caveats: Only applies if the calendar decision lands on Google; the iCloud path would need a different overlap script.
An overlap is not always a problem (both parents at the same recital). Without a rule such as 'kid event with no driver tag' it will cry wolf.
Happy reports; it does not move or decline anything.
Whether phone calendars already warn about cross-person overlaps was not checked; if they do not, this is a gap the phone leaves open.

The notification policy (G001) drops a text sent outside the allowed hours or over the daily cap instead of holding it, and by then the script has recorded the overlap as seen. So the job runs only inside the allowed hours.

How Ohai's conflict check behaves in use; its feature page says it scans connected calendars, flags overlapping events and offers to reschedule, which goes further than Happy's report-only line.
Whether `gog calendar conflicts` works on calendars shared as free/busy only.

That phone calendars give no cross-person overlap warning: a web search in round 3 found no Google or Apple help page describing one, only forum posts, so it is still not settled by an official source.
Whether one job can announce to two recipients; the docs' examples show a single `--to` target.

Where each parent's work meetings live. The card's example turns on a work meeting; an employer's Google calendar can be shared outside the organisation only up to the level its administrator sets (Google's admin page lists free/busy only as the lowest level), and a work calendar that is not on Google cannot be read by gog at all.

demand_source.title: 5 ways Google parents are using Gemini
demand_source.supports: Google's own post describes parents using its assistant to list the kid-friendly activities near them and to build complete itineraries for family trips.

edits.how: One research sub-agent run via `sessions_spawn` with `runTimeoutSeconds`, composing `web_fetch`, the place lookup and `home_weather`; calendar free time crosses as date ranges only; the Friday 16:00 job reuses it. The place lookup is a tool on the research agent and one of two connections to Google's place data: the `goplaces` command that OpenClaw bundles a skill for, wrapped as a host-side stdio MCP with `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` and the home coordinates held in the wrapper, or Google's hosted Maps server (Grounding Lite), which the roadmap names. For a trip abroad the parent's own agent, not research, adds the paperwork line from the renewals table (F063) and fixed official links; passport dates and names are never handed to research.
depends_on: Place lookup for hours and ratings (formerly F021, now part of this entry): a Google Cloud project with billing switched on, a Places API key held in a host-side wrapper, and a budget alert
Decision: the bundled goplaces command or Google's hosted Maps server (Grounding Lite), which the roadmap names
home_weather plugin (exists); an hourly rain window needs F083
F009 calendar read, only to pass free dates as date ranges
F049 mailout, only for the emailed long version
F063 renewals table, only for the passport line on a trip abroad
caveats: Happy books and pays for nothing: the plan ends in links and the parents book.
Prices are best effort. Plain page reads fail on many booking, hotel and transport sites, so those come as links, and an admission price appears only when a page that could be read showed it.

The pieces arrive at different times: opening hours and ratings need the place lookup (formerly F021, now part of this entry and not built), an hour-by-hour rain line needs the weather upgrade (F083), the emailed long version needs mailout (F049) and the passport line needs the renewals table (F063). Until then the plan is built from web pages and the half-day forecast and comes back as a text.
Drive time is not part of the plan unless a route lookup is added with the place lookup.
Only ages, a place, a distance and free dates as ranges are meant to reach the research agent; that is an instruction to the parent's agent, not an enforced limit.

The paperwork line is a pointer, not a ruling. USAGov's page on travel documents for children (usa.gov/travel-documents-children) covers trips abroad and says a consent letter, preferably notarised, should come from the other parent when a child travels with one parent, and from both when the child travels with a guardian or alone. Entry rules differ by country and airline, and Happy certifies nothing.

A general assistant such as Gemini already drafts an itinerary from a typed prompt, as the Google post behind this card shows. Happy's version saves retyping the family's ages, free dates and home weather, and adds the paperwork line.

The roadmap's research milestone names Google's hosted Maps server (Grounding Lite) for place data, and OpenClaw bundles a skill for the goplaces command instead. Both read Google's place data and both need billing switched on, so one is chosen before building. Google's page says the hosted server's place search returns an AI-generated summary with place ids and Maps links and does not mention opening hours, so check first that it can answer 'is it open now?'.
For a one-off 'is it open now?' the maps app on a parent's phone is quicker and has live traffic. The place lookup is here as data for the plan, not as a separate thing to ask Happy.
unverified: Hotel and train price snapshots: no opened source shows these sites are readable logged-out; expect links instead of prices.
The weather plugin returns 12-hour periods today (read in ~/src/happy-config, not citable), so an hourly rain window needs the plugin change in F083.
The emailed long version depends on the mailout server (F049), not built.
Current Places and Routes prices and free allowances were not read.
goplaces is not installed, so its flags were checked against the bundled skill and the upstream README only.
Whether Grounding Lite is generally available or a preview: Google's page does not label it.
edits.safety: The research agent holds no family data: it is given ages, a place, a distance and free dates as ranges only (a prompt rule on the parent's agent, not an enforced limit), and it has no payment or booking tool. The paperwork line for a trip abroad uses passport dates and names, so the parent's own agent writes it and none of it is handed to research. Answers go only to the asking parent. The Google key and the home coordinates sit in the host-side wrapper, not in the prompt, and every place query goes to Google.

demand_source.title: Winter Weather | Ready.gov
demand_source.supports: The federal preparedness site tells households to pay attention to weather reports and warnings of freezing weather and winter storms and to sign up for their community's warning system.

edits.how: All are operator-created host command jobs (`--command-argv`) with no model call: a script fetches a public source, keeps seen ids in a state file and prints one templated line or `NO_REPLY`. Weather (F018): `nws-alerts.mjs` every 30 minutes polls the National Weather Service active-alerts feed for the home point and dedups on the alert id. Schedules and pages (F029, SRC-09): `ics-watch.mjs`, hourly in season, reads a team's subscription link and reports changed events in the next seven days; `watch-page.mjs` every 6 hours uses a site's feed when there is one, otherwise a plain https GET and a text hash. Recalls (SRC-03, SRC-04): `cpsc-recalls.mjs` daily and `fda-recalls.mjs` twice a day, matched locally against owned-item, allergen, staples and medicine keyword lists. The schedule, page and recall jobs are timed inside the allowed hours of the notification policy (G001); only the storm-alert job runs round the clock.
caveats: A parent cannot start a watch from chat: command jobs are created by the operator, so each new watch is a request to Tony.

None of these gives earlier notice than the source's own service: Apple's Weather app can notify about government alerts once that is switched on, the team app's push is faster for a same-day change, and both recall agencies offer their own sign-ups; Happy adds the match, the school-night line and one text to both parents.
Happy is down in a power cut or a network outage and FDA's own list does not carry every recall, so silence from a watch is never an all-clear and the phones' emergency alerts stay on.
With a shared state file the second parent's job finds nothing new and stays silent, so each parent's job keeps its own file or one job delivers to the parents' group chat.

Command jobs run on the Gateway host as the happy user, outside the sandbox, agent tool policy and OpenClaw's fetch guardrails, so the scripts check each address themselves (https, public host) and are reviewed like the rest of the config repo.
A team's subscription link is a bearer secret, so it sits in a file only the happy user can read and stays out of family.json5 if that file is committed.
A hash watch on a school or town page can fire on changes that do not matter, pages that need JavaScript are out of reach, and many school portals publish no feed.

The recall match is only as good as the family's lists (substring matching gives false positives and misses unlisted items), and meat and poultry recalls and cars are not covered; parents add VINs and car seats to NHTSA's own app.

The notification policy (G001) drops a text sent outside the allowed hours or over the daily cap instead of holding it, and by then the script has recorded the item as seen, so a change found at night would never be told. The schedule, page and recall scripts therefore run only inside the allowed hours, and the storm alert is put in the class that passes quiet hours.
depends_on: G001 notification policy (the storm alert in the class that passes quiet hours; the other watches timed inside the allowed hours)
One job per parent with its own state file, or one job delivering to the parents' group chat (F006)
F009 family calendar read-only and decision 4 (Google or iCloud calendar), only for showing a team schedule in calendar answers
A first check of which of the family's school, town, library and camp sites publish a feed
For the recall watch: the home systems registry in F043 or a hand-kept owned-items list, and allergen, staples and medicine keyword lists in family.json5

demand_source.title: Double dosing: What to do if you take too much | Poison Control (National Capital Poison Center)
demand_source.supports: A poison centre lists medicine given by more than one person who do not communicate as a cause of double dosing and advises keeping a log that is marked each time a dose is given.

caveats: This is a log, not a clinician. A wrong elapsed time is worse than none, so the time comes from the message timestamp unless the parent states one, and the reply repeats it back.

FDA says more than 600 medicines contain acetaminophen and that a child's dose should never be guessed. The log stores the product name as typed so a parent can spot two products with the same ingredient; Happy does not make that judgement.
Child health notes pass through a cloud model under store:false. Use a nickname or initial and keep diagnoses out.

A note the two parents share on their phones already gives both of them one log: Apple's support page (support.apple.com/en-us/102462) says people with Apple devices can collaborate on a note. Such a note also works when Happy is down and keeps the child's health notes away from a cloud model. What Happy adds is the elapsed time worked out in code, the fixed check-the-label line and the sick-day add-ons (the absence-note draft, tomorrow's cancellations, the check-in reminder).

The same poison centre page says the log should stay with the medicine and be marked at every dose. Happy's log is not next to the bottle and cannot be reached when Happy or the network is down, so it works beside a note kept with the medicine and does not replace one.
unverified: Whether Apple's Health app could serve as the shared dose log. Apple's Medications page (support.apple.com/en-us/105064) says a person who shares health data can include which medications they take, and that Medications is not available with Apple Watch For Your Kids; it does not describe two parents logging doses for a child, so it is not shown to replace this log.
Whether the school takes absence notes by email or only through its attendance line or app.
Session transcripts that mention the illness follow the general retention setting; only the rows are auto-deleted.
